subject: Medicore private deploy: bundle structure, platform fee and credit trade-offs
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Janelle Park <janelle.park@medicore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-28 09:12 PDT
Subject: Medicore private deploy: bundle structure, platform fee and credit trade-offs

Hi Janelle —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Per our discussion, I wanted to follow up with a concise set of options for the private deployment (VPC) commercial construct so procurement can evaluate pricing versus operational guarantees. High level ask from your side: a) reduce first-year cash outlay, b) preserve SLO-backed response times, and c) keep an exit path after 12 months.

Quick summary of what we propose to share (Marissa is attaching a spreadsheet with line items):
- Option A (Commit-forward): Annual commit (12 months) with 20% platform fee + operator license bundle, 10% migration credit applied at invoice. Predictable unit pricing, lower per-token cost.
- Option B (Starter + Surge): Lower base commit (6 months) + burst credits you purchase as needed; higher platform fee (28%) but includes a 1-month SRE retainer.
- Option C (Pilot-first): 3-month pilot (metered) with implementation SOW and one-time onboarding credit; pilot converts to a committed rate if you exercise conversion.

Can Marissa and David weigh in with the numbers and a recommended path for a hospital system (moderate peak-burst usage, strong compliance requirements)? Janelle — if you can share an internal preferred split (commit vs. flexible) or a target ARR range, we can model a fitted counter.

Thanks,
Tessa

Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Janelle Park <janelle.park@medicore.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@medicore.com>
Date: 2025-07-28 10:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Medicore private deploy: bundle structure, platform fee and credit trade-offs

Tessa —

Appreciate the clear options. A few quick data points from procurement:
- Our target first-year spend (budgeted) is ~$900k ARR for the platform, but we need a cap on the initial invoice.
- We expect seasonal peaks (claims ingestion) in Q4 where burst capacity could double sustained throughput for ~3 weeks.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + custom logging retention for 18 months is required.

From a commercial lens, we prefer Option B (Starter + Surge) but need the platform fee reduced if we commit to a 9-month minimum (not 6). Also, we want a replaceable SRE retainer line item (we want the option to use our MSP for certain tasks). Is that something you can price and put into the spreadsheet?

Janelle
Director, Procurement
Medicore Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Janelle Park <janelle.park@medicore.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-28 15:40 PDT
Subject: Re: Medicore private deploy: bundle structure, platform fee and credit trade-offs

Hi Janelle — attaching detailed workbook (PrivDeploy_Bundle_v2.xlsx) and SOW terms (PrivDeploy_SOW_terms.pdf). Pulling the salient numbers here to keep the thread short:

Option A — Commit-forward (12 months)
- Annual commit: $1,100,000 ARR (baseline nodes + burst pool)
- Platform fee: 20% of committed ARR (billed monthly)
- Migration credit: 10% applied to first invoice ($110k)
- Operator licenses: included for up to 10 named operators, additional seat $3k/seat/yr
- Compliance add-on (18m log retention): one-time $25k legal/engineering setup + $5k/mo storage
- Conversion to lower per-token rates after 6 months if usage stabilizes.

Option B — Starter + Surge (9-month min requested)
- Base commit (9 mo): $450,000 (covers baseline site + small cache)
- Platform fee: 24% (if 9 mo); 28% if 6 mo
- Burst credits: pre-purchase block of 200k token-hours at $X/hour (modeled in workbook)
- SRE retainer: $40k/mo included in Option B (can be toggled off if you want MSP to provide tasks; reduction of $18k/mo if MSP covers runbook tasks)
- Pilot-to-commit conversion discount: one-time credit equal to 5% of the first committed invoice upon conversion.

Option C — Pilot-first (3 months)
- Metered rate: $/token + $15k onboarding fee (reimbursable if you convert)
- No platform fee during pilot; standard platform fee applies after conversion.

Notes:
- We can provide SOC2 evidence and a tailored logging SLA; Irene (cc'd) will own the compliance documentation handoff.
- Attachments: implementation-timeline.png shows a 10-week rollout for Option B (including staging and verification).

If you confirm preference for Option B (9 months + MSP substitution), we can draft a starter SOW and a short contract addendum that allows MSP substitution with a nominal audit/enablement fee ($12k).

Thanks — sharing workbook now.
Marissa
Sr. Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: PrivDeploy_Bundle_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), PrivDeploy_SOW_terms.pdf (pdf), implementation-timeline.png (image)

Subject: Re: Medicore private deploy: bundle structure, platform fee and credit trade-offs

Marissa / Tessa —

Thanks for the breakdown. A couple negotiation points from the technical procurement side: 
1) Burst credits: can we get a guaranteed holdback so credits are available at peak without needing prepayment? A small standby fee is acceptable.
2) SRE retainer: we will likely use our MSP for day-to-day ops but want Redwood to guarantee escalation and platform fixes. Can you carve SRE into an escalation-only retainer at $12k/mo plus per-incident engineering rates?

Procurement also asked for an invoice cap for the first quarter (no single invoice > $250k).

Tom
VP, Engineering Operations
Medicore Health

Hi all —

Operationally, two practical alternatives that balance your cap and burst needs:

Option B1 (Hybrid standby):
- 9-month base commit at $450k (as above)
- Standby burst pool: 20% of burst capacity held for you; standby fee = $8k/month (guarantees access when peak starts)
- Platform fee: 22% (compromise)
- MSP substitution: $9k one-time audit + $6k/mo enablement while MSP ramps; Redwood retains escalation-only retainer at $12k/mo.

Option B2 (Prepaid burst cushion):
- Same 9-month base commit
- Prepaid burst block scaled to your Q4 forecast; we amortize cost across monthly invoices to avoid large first-quarter invoice spikes (keeps any invoice <= $250k).
- Platform fee: 21% if prepaid burst is accepted.

If Medicore picks B1 we can fast-track SOW and include a 30-day conversion clause to a 12-month commit with an additional 7% credit on the first year committed amount. That gives you the exit path you asked for. Irene will prepare the SOC2/logging handoff checklist and include the 18-month retention pricing as line items.

Let me know which of B1/B2 you want modeled and we'll produce a redline-ready term sheet.

-David

David Kim
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference

Janelle / Tom —

Appreciate the quick feedback. Next steps we propose:
1) Medicore to confirm B1 (Hybrid standby) vs B2 (Prepaid cushion) by EOD Monday 8/4 so procurement has figures for the August finance review.
2) If B1 chosen: Redwood will prepare a starter SOW + 9-month MSA addendum that includes the standby fee and MSP substitution audit clause.
3) We will cap any single invoice in Q1 to $250k by amortizing prepaid items as David suggested.
4) Irene will share SOC2 evidence bundle and the logging retention estimate by EOD Friday.

If this sounds good, Janelle please confirm B1 or B2 and whether MSP substitution is required. Once we have that, Marissa will produce a redline-ready commercial term sheet and I will loop Legal to start a short addendum so you can get this into your supplier review.

Best,
Tessa
